content: 1. Buprenorphine (long-acting injection): Elagolix may reduce the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of buprenorphine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. If co-administered, monitor CYP3A substrates and consider increasing their dosage if necessary. 2. Buspirone: Elagolix may decrease the levels or effects of buspirone by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy as needed and monitor closely. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates during co-administration and consider dose adjustments. 3. Busulfan: Elagolix may reduce the levels or efficacy of busulfan by increasing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are advised. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates and adjust doses as required. 4. Butabarbital and Butalbital: Both butabarbital and butalbital may decrease the levels or effects of elagolix by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Therapy adjustments may be necessary. 5. Cabozantinib: Elagolix may lower the levels or effects of cabozantinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates and consider dose increases if needed. 6. Calcifediol and Calcitriol: Elagolix may reduce the levels or effects of calcifediol and calcitriol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are advised. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates and adjust doses as necessary. 7. Capivasertib: Elagolix may significantly reduce the levels or effects of capivasertib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Strong or moderate CYP3A inducers can reduce capivasertib exposure, potentially diminishing its efficacy. 8. Carbamazepine: Elagolix may decrease the levels or effects of carbamazepine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. Conversely, carbamazepine may reduce the levels or effects of elagolix. Avoid co-administration unless the benefits outweigh the risks. 9. Carfilzomib: Elagolix may increase the levels or effects of carfilzomib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Cariprazine: Elagolix may reduce the levels or effects of cariprazine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates and adjust doses as needed. 11. Carisoprodol: Elagolix may increase the levels or effects of carisoprodol by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are advised. Elagolix is a weak CYP2C19 inhibitor. Use caution with sensitive CYP2C19 substrates. 12. Carvedilol: Elagolix may increase the levels or effects of carvedilol by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Ceftobiprole Medocaril Sodium: Ceftobiprole may increase the levels or effects of elagolix by inhibiting OATP1B1/1B3 transporters. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of elevated plasma concentrations of OATP1B1/1B3 substrates. 14. Cenobamate: Cenobamate may reduce the levels or effects of elagolix by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. Additionally, cenobamate may decrease the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate. Increase the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed when co-administered with cenobamate. 15. Ceritinib: Elagolix may increase the levels or effects of ceritinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Conversely, elagolix may reduce ceritinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are advised. 16. Cetirizine: Elagolix may increase the levels or effects of cetirizine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Chloramphenicol: Chloramphenicol may increase the levels or effects of elagolix by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 18. Chlordiazepoxide: Elagolix may reduce the levels or effects of chlordiazepoxide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are advised. 19. Chloroquine: Elagolix may decrease the levels or effects of chloroquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 20. Chlorpheniramine: Elagolix may reduce the levels or effects of chlorpheniramine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are advised.
